content.text: MOA: stim prolif & diff of RBC precursors ->↑Hgb Synth -> faster retic into blood
Endogenous EPO: nephron prod (↓nephron mass -> ↓EPO -> anemia)
Clin Use: anemia from ESA-responsive Eti
Fever, HA, Myalgias                                                 -    GI effects, CP
death, MI, CVA, other serious CV events         -    Inj site pain
CKD: ↑risk death, serious adverse CV rxn, & CVA <- Hb  ±11
All hgb targets, ESA dose, or dosing strategy ↑risks
CA pt (breast, non-small cell lung, head & neck, lymphoid, cervical): ESAs shorten overall survival &/or ↑tumor progress or recurr
d/c post-chemo, ⍉ESA + myelosuppress chemotx if will cure
use lowest ESA dose to ⍉RBC transfusions & serious CV/thromboembolic rxn
Rx=enroll in/comply w ESA APPRISE Oncology Program
Monitoring:      -    Hgb     -    Serum ferritin       -    Transferrin sat       -    BP
Upper safety limits: 10 g/dL: pt ⍉dialysis, 11 g/dL: pt dialysis
Tx w ESA -> ↑Fe demand SO during use of ESA tx, maintain:
All pt who receive ESA must be provided w med guide
Clin Use: Pre-op: DVT prophylaxis when used
: glycoprotein manufactured thru recombinant DNA technology and has the same actions as EPO

: chemotherapy-induced anemia, anemia assoc w/ CKD, anemia ← zidovudine, pediatric anemia in children undergoing dialysis for CKD, reduction of allogenic blood transfusion in surg (elective, noncardiac, nonvascular) pts @ ↑risk for perioperative transfusion w sig, anticipated blood loss
: CKD (↑BP, HA, arthralgias, nausea), HIV (fever, fatigue, HA, cough, diarrhea, rash, nausea, skin rxns, congestion, dizziness), allergic rxns
: anemia assoc w/ CKD both on & off dialysis, anemia in pts w/ ⍉myeloid malignancies where anemia = ← the effect of concomitantly administered chemo

: pts treated w ESA and dosed to a target hgb concentration of 13.5 g/dL were @ a significantly ↑risk for serious and life-threatening CV comp (death, MI, hsp for CHF, CVA) compared to pts dosed to a target Hb of 11.3 g/dL – FDA recommends a target Hb in the range 10-12 g/dL and ⍉ to exceed 12 g/dL; pts have an ↑risk of serious CV events and death when these prod are dosed to target Hb > 12 g/dL

: in CA pts w certain tumor types (ie, breast, non-small cell lung, head and neck, lymphoid, cervical), ESAs shortened overall survival and/or ↑the risk of tumor progression or recurr in some clin studies – in pts w CA, use the lowest ESA dose needed to ⍉RBC transfusions and serious cardiovasc and thromboembolic rxns

: use ESAs only for tx of anemia ← concomitant myelosuppressive chemo, and d/c following the completion of a chemo course – pts receiving myelosuppressive chemo should ⍉be treated w ESAs when the anticipated outcome = cure
